node.label: Jonathan Israel
node.description: A historian of the Dutch Republic, European Jewry and the Enlightenment whose radical-Enlightenment interpretation gives philosophical ideas a strong explanatory role. In a 2023 interview, Israel argues that the reception of Spinoza helped create a radical current committed to secularism, democratic republicanism and freedom of expression, which he opposes to a moderate Enlightenment. The coherence and reach of that current are disputed. Antoine Lilti stresses the diversity of the most heterodox Enlightenment writings and the ambiguity of ‘Spinozism’ as a historian’s category. David Bell credits Israel’s range and his insistence on ideas, but argues that he infers influence from similarity, takes passages out of context and overstates the ideological causes of the French Revolution.
